script.title: Chapter 26: Fire in the Pepper Fields

panels.description: Wide, full page width. Midday in the dry season, seen from the fort wall: parched scrub, low hills, a dark green belt of pepper country and palms to the north. On the far horizon, a thin, uncertain line of grey smoke. Nagoji at the parapet in three-quarter back view, one hand on the warm stone. He is Ananthan Pillai now: Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, European boots, silver chain of office; NOT a mundu. A Nair sentry beside him (white mundu, crossed leather belt), unconcerned, leaning on his spear.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: At first it looked like nothing more than the usual dry season burn.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A farmer clearing undergrowth. A careless coal from a cook fire.

panels.description: Narrow strip, same horizon, later. The line has thickened and broken, and now smoke rises in two separate places, far apart. Nagoji has straightened. The sentry has stopped leaning.

The war hall inside the fort. A long, low room with carved wooden pillars and a map table heaped with palm-leaf bundles around a hand-painted cloth map of the canal country (ink lines only, no lettering or labels). Padmini Amma (older now, grey through her coiled black hair, lined face, still upright, simple gold, cotton sari hitched for walking, long walking stick) mid-argument across the table with Ramayyan Dalawa (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth, stylus in hand). Marthanda Varma (V13 face; cream and gold, bare-headed, his hair in a side knot above his left ear, no turban, no crest, gold necklaces, bare-chested, a spear leaning beside him) on a low platform behind them. Nagoji already in the room, by a pillar at the table's edge (Kerala topknot, NO turban, white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain of office). The one action: in the main doorway a runner bursts in, bare chest slick with sweat, and every head turns to him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Padmini Amma had come to the fort that morning to argue over grain rates and levy schedules.

copy.speaker: RUNNER
copy.text: Raiders! From the west and the north.

panels.description: The runner down on one knee, panting, one hand on the floor. In the foreground, out of focus, only the foot of a walking stick, stopped mid-tap an inch above the floor. No other figure in frame.

copy.speaker: RUNNER
copy.text: Some with Dutch guns. Some with old house banners.

copy.speaker: RUNNER
copy.text: They strike near Padmini Amma's upper fields.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Close on Padmini, turning slowly toward the runner. The men around her are soft and blurred. She is very calm, and that is worse than shouting.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: They chose my fields. Of course they did.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Old men fight their wars in land they have never walked; young ones set torches where women count vines.

panels.description: Ramayyan, fingers pinching the bridge of his nose, palm leaves spread before him, stylus laid down.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Two fronts. Exactly what Ramayyan had feared.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The timing is not an accident.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Someone has been counting our drills as carefully as we count their gossip.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The northern column was Kollamkara's, bold with whispers of Dutch backing.

panels.description: Wide. The strip as Nagoji pictures it, an aerial view painted like a map coming alive, no figures and no lettering or labels: dense green walls of pepper vines climbing rough bark support posts on both sides of a narrow path; a canal running alongside with low boats; small shrines of stone and carved wood almost swallowed by foliage on the ridges. Two faint smoke trails converge on it, one from the coast, one from the northern hills.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: We cannot let them hold that strip. If they do, they have a knife at our throat.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I saw the problem as soon as I pictured the map.

panels.description: Back in the hall. Nagoji at the table, finger on the cloth map where the path narrows (map drawn in ink lines only: canal, path, ridges; no lettering or labels). Ramayyan opposite him.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Our horse cannot move at speed through those vines. The path is too narrow. The canal banks too soft.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Foot.

panels.description: Nagoji shaking his head, eyes still on the map. Varma behind, leaning forward on his platform.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Foot will bleed in every bush. Every tree hides a musket. We will lose men in inches.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You have an alternative?

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Tight on Nagoji, lit from the side. Behind him, through a window slit, the two smudges of smoke on the horizon. He does not look like a man who has had a good idea.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The answer came before I wanted it to.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Burn it.

panels.description: Wide. The whole hall gone still. Padmini's head has snapped toward Nagoji. Ramayyan's stylus has stopped above the leaf. Varma does not move. The runner, still kneeling, looks from face to face.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The word hung in the air like smoke.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (small, soft lettering)
copy.text: Burn it?

panels.description: Nagoji leaning over the map table, tracing a thin zig zag along the canal with one finger (map drawn in ink lines only: canal, path, ridges; no lettering or labels). Quick, as if speed could make it smaller.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Not all. A strip. Narrow. Enough to deprive them of cover along the canal.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Then they must choose. Retreat into the open where our horse can run, or stay and be flanked in smaller patches.

panels.description: Two-shot across the table: Padmini standing with her stick, Nagoji straightening to face her.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You speak of my vines as if they were scrub.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Today, to them, they are a shield. Tomorrow, if they live, they are coin.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I know what I am asking.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Tight on Padmini's hand on the head of her stick, knuckles tightening. Her face above it, eyes fixed on him.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You know.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You do not feel.

panels.description: Varma on his platform, looking between Nagoji and Padmini. His voice is quiet; the room leans in to hear it. He reaches down with his spear and drags its tip slowly along the canal on the cloth map, toward the small drawn fort marks (ink lines only, no lettering or labels).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If we do nothing, they will move along that corridor until they reach places where our walls are thin and our men few.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: They will write their own terms in our fields.

panels.description: Padmini turning to face the king.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: If we burn, you carve a wound through my land that will take years to heal.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Pepper is not rice. It does not spring back in one season. You cut into my children and their children.

panels.description: Ramayyan, his stylus lying still on the leaf, looking up at her gently. Small inset in the lower corner: Padmini's eyes, closed.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Amma, if we let them keep that corridor, they carve different wounds.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Through forts. Through houses. Through your own name, when they brag of having used your land to break the king.

panels.description: Full width. Padmini, eyes open now, wet and furious, standing straight and bringing her stick down hard on the floor, the tap that stopped on page 1 finally landing. She faces all three men at once.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Do it.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: But do not pretend you did it to me without my consent.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Let every man who walks that blackened line in years to come know that I allowed it, and that I remember every step you take on it.

panels.description: Nagoji, a single nod. His throat is tight and his jaw is set.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I will ride there myself.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I will not ask another to light the first torch.

panels.description: Wide. A column of riders on a dry red road. Nagoji at the head on Kayal, his bay mare with the ochre red-brown coat of earth after rain. Nagoji: Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud; long white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, European boots, silver chain of office, talwar at his hip; NOT a mundu. Half a length behind on his left, Ponnan on a smaller, lighter Maravar horse, a head lower: broad-shouldered, loose curly hair uncovered, no topknot, thick moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth over a short jacket, white mundu hitched above bare knees, a spear. The white coat leads the column. Behind them, Travancore riders in white mundu with crossed leather belts under a red standard with a silver conch. Ahead, dark greasy columns of smoke; sparks drifting in the air around the horses.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The ride to her upper fields was short and long at once.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Short in distance. Long in what it stretched inside me.

panels.description: Large, most of a tier. From the ridge, looking down: pepper vines in dense ordered lines along both sides of the canal, green fruit clusters hanging like beads; the narrow path running between them like a vein. Raiders (Kollamkara's house men: dark indigo or earth-brown cloth, head cloths, bare-chested, no cross-belts; NOT blue coats, NOT red coats) half hidden in the foliage, musket barrels glinting between leaves, small puffs of musket smoke from the shadows. Low, loaded boats on the canal. The riders reined in along the ridge in the foreground, in silhouette, beside a small shrine almost swallowed by leaves.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The sight below made my stomach knot.

panels.description: Ponnan (loose curly hair uncovered, no topknot, red shoulder cloth over a short jacket, white mundu hitched above bare knees, spear) leaning in from his smaller horse at the shoulder of Nagoji (Kerala topknot, NO turban, long white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain), who is already swinging down from Kayal, the ochre-bay mare.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: If we hit them from here, we expose ourselves. They have too many places to hide.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We do not hit them here.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We hit their shield.

panels.description: Nagoji on foot at the first row of vines, full figure: Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud; white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, European boots, silver chain of office, talwar at his hip. Crisp dry leaf litter under his boots. The vine line in front of him is untouched and green; the only smoke is the raiders', far off beyond the canal. A Travancore soldier (white mundu, crossed leather belt) hands him a torch, its head wrapped in oil-soaked cloth. Bleeding faintly into the smoke above him, smoke-textured rather than solid figures, like a stain rather than a clean flashback frame: on one side Padmini's face, grey in her coiled hair, the head of her stick beside it; on the other Revathi's face, grey threading her hair, jasmine in her braid, the tali at her throat.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: You will always choose the king first, Revathi had said. The houses later.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Tight: the torch held to the dry leaves and bark at the base of a support post. The flame touches. Nothing has caught yet. Nagoji's face behind the torch, lit orange, waiting.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a heartbeat, nothing happened.

panels.description: One standard tier, full width. The flame has caught. Fire crawls up the post and licks at the lower leaves; sap spits white steam from the stem. Nagoji, full figure, steps back from it, torch still raised, soot already on his white coat (red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches and European boots visible; Kerala topknot, NO turban).

High angle. A zig zag of separate fires along the line, with deliberate gaps between them. Nagoji (white coat, topknot) moving along it, Travancore men (white mundu, crossed leather belts) spreading out on either side of him, setting their torches to post after post.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A controlled burn, as much as such a thing can be in war.

panels.description: The fire jumping where no one meant it to: leaping a careful gap to catch a fallen branch, black smoke boiling up. Two Travancore men (white mundu, crossed leather belts) flinching back from the sudden heat.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Enough, I hoped, to deny full cover without turning the land into a charcoal scar with no hope.

panels.description: Travancore musketeers (Nair men in white mundu with crossed leather belts and matchlocks; NOT blue coats, NOT red coats) kneeling in a line at the edge of the burn, firing into the smoke. In the gaps they created, raiders show only as black silhouettes against the flame, head cloths and bare shoulders, no cross-belts.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: This was a cruel way to fight.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. One action. In the foreground the wind has shifted, and Nagoji, face streaked black, white coat smeared with soot, hauls one of his own men (a Travancore man in white mundu with a crossed leather belt) back out of the smoke by his shoulder cloth. Behind them, in the grey, raiders show only as coughing, stumbling silhouettes, arms over their faces. No bodies.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I do not pretend there was honour in that moment.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was ugly and hot and filled with the sounds of men and plants dying together.

panels.description: Wide, late afternoon. The corridor is gone: a blackened stretch of ground through the green, charred posts fallen, earth scorched. On both sides, untouched pepper still stands, leaves fluttering in the hot wind. In the foreground ash, a dropped musket and a scorched raiders' house banner (plain faded green cloth with a simple emblem, no writing). Far off, a few singed survivors limping into neighbouring land, one still wading out of the canal. No bodies.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We did not pursue far.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The fire had done its work.

panels.description: Wide. Night, the same war hall, lamplit, the map table in the middle. Marthanda Varma (V13 face; cream and gold, bare-headed, his hair in a side knot above his left ear, no turban, no crest, gold necklaces) on his low platform at the far end, watching. Sooty soldiers in white mundu sitting quiet along the walls. In the foreground Nagoji (Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud; white European-cut coat stained black at the cuffs, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, European boots, silver chain of office), lowering a brass cup from his lips with a grimace. In the side doorway behind him, Padmini, without ceremony: soot streaks on her sari, hair plastered to her temples with sweat, stick in hand. Every head in the hall is turning toward her.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That night the smell of smoke clung to everything. Even the water tasted of it.

panels.description: Padmini standing in the centre of the room by the map table, looking straight at Nagoji. Her voice is flat, and her face is flatter. Varma a lamplit shape on his platform behind her.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You did what you said you would. You burned a strip. Not all. Enough.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: I rode there. I walked the black line. It runs like a mark across my land.

panels.description: Two-shot across the map table: Padmini unmoving, Nagoji answering her.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: For years, men will ask what happened there. I will tell them. They will ask why. I will tell them that too.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We stopped them. They will not use your vines as cover again.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Nagoji, close. She has not answered him, and he has heard how thin his answer was. He does not look away.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: When the raiders burned your lower fields years ago, you called it an act of cowardice.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Today, I did it with a torch in my own hand. I do not know which ash is heavier.

panels.description: Padmini, eyes hard and unblinking. She rubs a smear of soot from her sari between finger and thumb and lets it fall onto the cloth map, onto the canal where Nagoji traced the strip on page 3 (ink lines only, no lettering or labels).

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: They burned to destroy. You burned to save.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: But ash tastes the same in my mouth, Ananthan. Do not expect me to distinguish the flavour.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (after a breath, a separate balloon)
copy.text: I do not say you were wrong.

panels.description: Reverse angle, over Padmini's shoulder onto Nagoji's face as he takes it. Her voice drops; this is harder for her than the anger.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: If I thought there had been another way, I would be screaming now, not speaking.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: But do not expect me to thank you. There are wounds that are necessary and wounds that are kind. This was the first, not the second.

panels.description: Varma on his platform, face unreadable. Padmini half-turned toward him, leaning on her stick.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You have my word that the state will help replant.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Your word does not make plants grow faster.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: But perhaps it will keep some of my boys from having to sell their swords to men like Kollamkara when the hunger comes.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Padmini at the doorway with her back to the hall, paused, not looking round. Nagoji small in the lamplight behind her.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You have chosen your side firmly now, Pillai.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: When Dutch, Mysore or your own hills come in force, you will be in front of the king's fort. You will not be standing on my verandah.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: I will remember that.

panels.description: Wide. The fort wall at evening, a few days later. Far off, the blackened strip still visible as a dark line across the green. Nagoji alone at the parapet (Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud; white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, European boots, silver chain of office; NOT a mundu). Revathi Bayi (a little younger than Nagoji; deep indigo sari with gold, jasmine in her braid, grey threading her hair, tali at her throat, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line at the hairline) coming along the wall walk toward him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Revathi's anger arrived a few evenings later, as I had known it would.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You carved your own mark into this land.

panels.description: Nagoji turning to her. She has not stopped walking.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We carved it together. The king, Ramayyan, Padmini. I merely held the first torch.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Men like you always say that. You hide behind councils and shared decisions when the fire is yours.

panels.description: Revathi leaning on the parapet beside Nagoji, staring north at the strip. Neither looks at the other.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: If a Dutchman had done what you did, you would have called him monster.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Because you did it for a king you respect, you call it necessity.

panels.description: Small panel. Nagoji, turned toward her profile.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You think there was another choice?

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Revathi still facing the horizon after a long silence, the last light on her face. Nagoji at the edge of frame, watching her.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: No.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: That is what angers me most. Sometimes, the only choices left are between a slow death and a quick burn.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You chose well for the kingdom. Badly for the house. As I knew you would.

panels.description: Revathi straightening from the parapet and facing him fully.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: This does not make you evil. It makes you dangerous.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: To love you, as I do, is to love a man whose first instinct is to save the larger pattern, not the smaller square.

panels.description: Two-shot, Revathi and Nagoji. Her gaze flicks toward the blackened strip, then back to him.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You once asked only for a corner of my house and a sliver of my heart. Today you carved a wound across my land instead.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You knew that before we stood before the goddess.

panels.description: Revathi stepping away from the parapet, answering over her shoulder without stopping. Nagoji stays where he is.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Of course. I married you with my eyes open.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I knew there would be days when you stood on the wall beside the king instead of on my verandah. I did not expect to like it when those days came.

panels.description: Seen past Nagoji's shoulder at the parapet: Revathi, a few paces off along the wall walk, turns back halfway, her face in the last light, one hand at the tali.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: We will work together when it suits the land. We will stand in the same halls. We will share this house in name and in law.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: But do not ask me to pretend this scar is not also your work.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Revathi walking away along the wall walk, her back straight, already small. Nagoji alone and small at the parapet, the evening sky reddening over the walls.

Wide, long lens, sunset. No figures. The burned strip across the green: scorched posts standing as jagged black silhouettes against a red sky, the dark vein of ash running between untouched pepper on both sides.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The fire in the pepper fields had done more than deny cover to raiders.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It had burned away the illusion that love could soften the choices ahead.

panels.description: A canal bank at dusk. Bales of cloth stacked by a moored boat. Ibrahim Marakkar (a stocky, broad-chested coastal Muslim broker; short coat over a vest with bulging pockets; scar from his LEFT ear to the jaw) in three-quarter view showing his anatomical left side, the scar clearly visible, talking quietly with a man seen from behind, in shadow.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Later, when Ramayyan sifted rumours, Ibrahim Marakkar's name floated more than once to the surface.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Whether he had helped Kollamkara reach Dutch guns or had nudged those same whispers toward the fort first was never entirely clear.

panels.description: The war hall by day. Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) at his palm leaves, not looking up, stylus moving. Nagoji standing across the table (Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud; white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, European boots, silver chain of office; NOT a mundu).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I asked Ramayyan about it once, months after the ash had cooled.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Some men are most useful when both sides believe they are theirs.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Do not trouble yourself with his accounts. I keep them for him.

panels.description: Two-shot across the table. Nagoji leaning in. Ramayyan still does not look up.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And if he betrayed us?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Then I would know. And he would know that I know. That is usually enough.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Tight on Ramayyan's hand turning a palm leaf, stylus already moving to the next line. A small brass dish of dried black peppercorns weighs down the stack of finished leaves.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Men like Ibrahim rarely walked in straight lines.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Perhaps that was the only way to survive on a coast where every power wanted the same pepper.

frames.review_note: Small problems only. The silver chain of office hangs in a long loop down his back, so it looks worn back to front. The smoke is a row of several small plumes rather than one thin line, but it still reads as a distant line on the horizon. The sentry also has a topknot and moustache, but his mundu and crossed belts keep him distinct from Nagoji. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch26 row: topknot, grey at the temples, curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, white coat over a red waistcoat with brass buttons, breeches and boots. There is no text in the art, and the open sky on the upper right takes both captions easily.

Minor only. Nagoji leans forward with both hands on the parapet instead of standing fully straight, but the alert posture still carries the beat. The sentry has stopped leaning, and two separate smoke columns stand far apart on the same horizon as 1.1. The tiled guard-house roof matches 1.1. Nagoji matches his sheet and bible row: topknot with no turban, grey temples, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. There is faint stipple on his jaw, but the chin reads clean-shaven. The sentry also has a topknot and moustache, like Nagoji, but his bare chest, crossed belts and mundu keep them distinct. The panel has no lettering. There is no painted text.

Small problems only. Ramayyan still faces Padmini with his stylus and has his back to the doorway, so only three of the four heads turn to the runner. Varma's hair knot sits at the back of his crown rather than above his left ear. Nagoji's ear stud reads pale rather than gold. Ramayyan shows a faint moustache that is not on his sheet. Otherwise the whole cast is present and on model: Padmini with grey in her coiled hair, gold, sari and stick; Ramayyan with receding hair, white cloth, stylus and palm leaves; Varma bare-headed and bare-chested in gold necklaces on the platform, spear beside him; Nagoji by a pillar in coat, red waistcoat and chain. The sweat-slick runner bursts through the main doorway. The cloth map has ink lines and no lettering. The lamps are brass with open wicks. Lettering placement: the caption can sit over the roof tiles at top centre, and the runner's balloon over the door lintel at top right.

Minor only. The foreground stick foot is drawn sharp instead of out of focus. It still hovers above the floor with its shadow below, so the 'stopped mid-tap' beat reads. Its rough bark texture matches Padmini's sheet but is rougher than the polished stick in 1.5. The floor has a glossy, slightly photographic finish. The runner matches 1.3: curly hair, moustache, sweat-slick bare chest and white loincloth. He kneels on his right knee with his right hand flat on the floor and his left foot planted. The anatomy is sound. The setting matches 1.3: dark carved pillars, brass lamps and an open doorway onto palms. There is no painted text. Lettering space: the plain dark wall and ceiling above the doorway (about x 0.31-0.62, y 0.02-0.19), with the empty lower floor as a second option.

Minor only. The men behind Padmini are only slightly softer than she is, not as soft and blurred as the script asks, but she clearly dominates and turns toward the runner, whose wet shoulder is at the right edge. Varma's hair is in a knot at the back rather than clearly above his left ear, and he wears a gold-bordered cloth over one shoulder that he did not have in 1.3. He is correctly bare-headed, with no turban or crest. Her stick is polished carved wood here, while in 1.4 it is rough bark. Padmini matches her sheet: grey through her black hair, a coil at the nape, gold ear studs, a gold neck ring, a cream sari with a gold border and no blouse. Her hand on the stick is well drawn. Nagoji is correct: topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, coat, waistcoat and chain. Ramayyan matches his sheet. The map is ink lines only, with no lettering. Lettering space: the roof and plain wall band across the upper middle and right (about x 0.45-0.9, y 0.0-0.25), above Ramayyan's and Varma's heads.

Minor: Varma's dais is visible and empty in the centre background. In 1.3 he sits on it, and in 2.4 he leans forward on his platform, so it reads as if he has stood up. Otherwise clean. Ramayyan matches his sheet (receding hair, curly black sides, thin fine features, plain white cloth). The beat is exact: he pinches the bridge of his nose, palm leaves are spread and the stylus is laid down. The map is ink lines and dots with no lettering. Hands are sound. There is ample lettering space on the plain upper wall (x 0.40-0.80, y 0.02-0.33) and over the lower-right map area.

Clean. It is a figureless high-angle view: pepper vines on rough posts on both sides of a narrow path, a canal with low cargo boats, and two small shrines half swallowed by foliage on the ridge. Two smoke trails rise, one from the northern hills and one from the coast. No figures (the boats are empty), no lettering and no anachronism. The lettering can sit in the sky band at the top and on the low-detail distant plain and sea at upper right. Varma is speaking off-panel from the hall, so his tail goes to the top edge.

Minor only. Ramayyan sits to the right across the table corner rather than squarely opposite. The ink-line map matches the script for 2.3, but 1.3 and 2.4 show a coloured map, so the map style varies across the page. Everything else matches: Nagoji in uniform (white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain, Kerala topknot with grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud), Ramayyan matches his sheet with stylus and palm leaves, hands are sound, there is no lettering on the map, and the plain wall and roof at the top leave room for both balloons.

Minor only. Nagoji's head is bowed toward the map, which reads as brooding more than actively shaking his head, but it still fits the beat. Three turbaned guards stand in the background; the script does not call for them, but they suit the war hall. Lettering space is acceptable but moderate. The plain wall above the left guard (upper left) can take Nagoji's medium balloon, and the wall with window slits at upper right can take Varma's short one. Nagoji matches his sheet and the bible: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold stud, topknot with grey temples, white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain of office, riding boots and the scar on his left forearm. Varma matches too: bare-headed with a side knot above his left ear, bare-chested, cream mundu with gold border, gold necklaces and a spear by the platform. His hands are sound on the rail. The map is drawn in ink lines only, with no lettering anywhere.

Minor only. The window is a tall barred opening rather than a narrow slit, and the rough stone-block wall differs from the plastered hall walls in 2.3 and 2.4, but the shot is tight enough to read as another corner of the fort. His fist covers his mouth and most of his chin; the visible jaw shows only faint ink texture, not a beard. Tight on Nagoji, lit from the side, two smoke columns on the horizon through the window, and a brooding expression that fits the beat. The uniform, topknot, grey temples, curled moustache and gold stud all match, and the hand is sound. The dark upper-left wall and the sky at upper right leave plenty of room for the caption and the 'Burn it.' balloon.

Minor only: the kneeling runner named in the art direction is not in frame (the hall-gone-still beat is still clear: Padmini's head snapped to Nagoji, Ramayyan and Varma frozen, guards at the doors). Varma's hair is a crown knot rather than the bible's side knot above the left ear, but this matches 1.3 and 2.4. Nagoji's breeches read as long trousers tucked into tall boots. Ramayyan's stylus rests on the leaf instead of hovering above it. Nagoji's face, stud, clean chin, uniform and the white scar on his left forearm are correct. The map is ink and wash only, with no lettering. Caption can sit top left over the roof beams and doorway; Padmini's small balloon fits on the dark wall between her head and Varma.

Minor only. This fixes every r1 problem. The brand on the inner left forearm is now a pale, puckered patch beside one long white scar, with no symbol or outline. The map is ink lines only (canal, dotted path, ridges, tiny trees) with no letters or pseudo-labels near the finger. There is no belt over the waistcoat. The doorway guards wear white head cloths and crossed belts, as in 3.1. Varma is seated on his dais at the right instead of an empty seat. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch26 row: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain. Both hands are sound, with the right index finger tracing the canal and the left palm flat. Small slips: Varma's hair is loose to the shoulders rather than in a knot, though he is small in the background. The map is plain ink while 3.1 and 3.3 show a colour-washed map, but the script asks for ink lines here. Both Nagoji balloons fit on the rafters and the cream wall at upper right, between the central pillar and Varma's window, or over the ceiling at upper left.

Acceptable, with background continuity slips worth noting. The r1 tattoo problem is gone: both of Nagoji's sleeves are down, so no forearm mark shows. The beat works. It is a two-shot across the map table: Padmini at left with her stick, grey threading through hair coiled at the nape, gold stud earrings and necklace, and the cream gold-bordered sari in the old drape with no blouse. Nagoji at right leans on the table and faces her in profile. He has his topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, white coat, red waistcoat, chain and sword. All four hands are sound. The map has no lettering and the red banner is plain. Slips: (1) The royal seat with its red bolster stands empty in the centre background. Varma sits there in 3.1, 3.2 and 4.1, though 3.4 (already kept) has the same empty dais in soft focus. (2) The background guards wear red turbans and red waist sashes. In 3.1 and 3.2 they wear white head cloths and crossed belts. (3) The map is colour-washed, which matches 3.1 but not the ink map in 3.2. (4) Nagoji is still leaning on both palms rather than fully straightened. None of these breaks a principal, the beat or a hard rule. All three balloons fit on the plain cream wall between the pillars at top centre: Padmini's on the left half, Nagoji's two on the right half, with the rafters above as overflow.

Minor only: in the soft background at right, a dais with a cushion and a spear beside it is empty, a small continuity slip against Varma being present in 3.1 and 4.1. A tiny pen-like scribble on the curled corner of the background map (about 20 px, near x 0.85, y 0.95) could be cleaned in retouch. Otherwise it matches the beat: tight on her large, anatomically sound fist clenched on the head of the stick, her face above it, eyes fixed on Nagoji off-panel right. She has grey threading, gold earrings, necklace and bangle, and the cream gold-bordered sari with no blouse. Both balloons fit on the rafters and wall at upper left, or on the plain wall at right between the window slits.

Small problems only. Varma matches the V13 face: moustache, red tilak, pearl ear drop, bare-headed, bare-chested, cream gold-bordered mundu, gold necklaces. His knot sits at the back right of his head, not above the left ear. This is close to the crown knot already accepted in 3.1. He stands right at the front edge of his platform, with the red-cushioned seat and his tall spear behind him. He drags the tip of a second, short spear along the canal toward the drawn fort mark. That short spear looks a little stubby, but the beat reads clearly. His eyes glance off-panel to the right. The crowd is gone. Only two small Nair guards with crossed belts stand by the doorway. The map is ink and wash only: palms, canal and fort outline, with no lettering. The hall, the light and the brass lamps match page 3 and 4.3. Both balloons fit on the plain back wall in the upper band, at upper left above the doorway or upper right beside his head.

Small problems only. Padmini matches her sheet and the ch26 row: grey threading in her coiled hair, gold ear studs and necklace, bangles, cream gold-bordered sari in the old drape with no blouse, and her rough walking stick. Her hands are sound. Her head and eyes turn sharply toward the right edge, where the king is off-panel. The empty platform is out of frame, and there are no extra people. The cloth map on the waist-high table shows only ink lines. A few faint, smudgy terrain scribbles near its top-right corner, around x 0.85 to 0.95 and y 0.70 to 0.78, read as hill hatching rather than letters. The hall matches 4.3: carved pillars, plain wall, slit window, brass lamps with open flames, and a sunlit doorway. A large plain wall in the upper right takes both balloons well clear of her face.

Usable. Ramayyan matches his sheet (receding hair, curly sides, plain white cloth, stylus held still over the palm-leaf bundle) and is looking up at Padmini. She matches her sheet with the grey threading. The requested lower-right inset of her closed eyes is present, with a thin painted inset border. There is no text on the map or the banners, the hall matches page 3, and there is no invented crowd. Minor points: Varma's platform behind Ramayyan is empty (a low seat with bolsters), as in 3.3 and 3.4 but not in 4.5. In the main image Padmini's eyes are open; the inset carries the closed eyes. Plain back wall in the upper centre has room for both Ramayyan balloons.

Small problems only. Padmini is on model: grey threading, gold, cream gold-bordered sari with no blouse. She leans in, faces the camera, and drives her stick hard into the floor with impact lines, her free hand in a fist. Her hands and feet are sound. Her eyes are furious but barely look wet. The invented foreground men are gone. Only two Nair guards with crossed belts stand by the side doorways, so the three men she addresses read as off-panel on the camera side. Continuity slips: Varma's platform behind her is empty, as in 4.3, which conflicts slightly with him standing at it in 4.1. Its seat here is a plain high-backed wooden chair, not the red-cushioned seat seen in 4.1. A small hatched hill cluster at the right end of the map, near x 0.66 and y 0.62, looks slightly like scribble but is not legible text. Hanging brass lamps have open flames. All three balloons fit on the dark back wall to the right of her head (about x 0.47 to 0.72, y 0.03 to 0.32), with the plain floor at lower right as overflow.

Small problems only. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, a clean chin, grey at the temples, a Kerala topknot with long curls, and a small gold ear stud. He wears the white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain of office, with both sleeves down and no brand or scar showing. Faint stubble shading along his jaw and chin could be lightened in retouch. A red cloth sash is wrapped around the waistcoat at the waist; that is not in the bible row or in 3.1, though it reads as part of the waistcoat, red on red. The coat has small shoulder tabs. His head dips in a nod with his eyes down and his jaw set, so the beat reads. The crowd is gone. In soft focus behind him, Varma sits on his platform, which fits the bible and 4.1. Here Varma has a gold-bordered cloth over one shoulder, and the two guards wear red waist sashes, both minor background differences. Brass wall lamps have open flames. The map shows only pictograms and the canal, with no lettering. Both balloons fit on the plain upper-right wall and roof, well clear of his face.

Acceptable with minor notes. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch25-27 uniform row: Kerala topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, white European coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain, talwar hilt, boots. Kayal is a bay with black mane, tail and lower legs, no white markings, ochre quilted pad, though her chest reads a little heavy. The column has a red standard with a silver conch, Travancore riders in white mundu with crossed belts, smoke columns and drifting sparks on a red road. No painted text. Minor issues: Ponnan rides on Nagoji's right, not his left (mirrored from the script). Ponnan wears a small gold ear stud of his own, which is Nagoji's identifier. Ponnan's hair is longer and his face leaner than the cropped-curl sheet. He has a foot in a dark shoe or boot. The smoke sits behind and to the right of the column rather than clearly ahead. Lettering: both captions fit in the open sky at the top left (x 0.20 to 0.45, y 0.02 to 0.14, between the standard and Nagoji's head). The smoke at the top right (x 0.65 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.15) also works. Neither spot covers a face.

Usable with minor deviations. The riders are painted in full colour instead of silhouette, only Nagoji and Ponnan are shown rather than the reined-in column, and the vantage is only slightly raised, so it reads less as looking down from a ridge. The raiders are also quite close to the riders. Everything else checks out: Nagoji matches in profile (topknot, grey, clean chin, moustache, stud, uniform, chain), Kayal is plain bay with no markings, and Ponnan is correct. The pepper rows, the bare-chested raiders in head cloths with musket smoke, the loaded boats on the canal and the small leaf-swallowed shrine all match the script. There is no painted text and no gore. The caption fits in the sky and distant-hill band across the top centre and right.

Usable with two minor gaps. Ponnan turns toward Nagoji from his own horse rather than leaning in at Nagoji's shoulder, and Nagoji is pressing on the saddle at the start of a dismount, not yet swinging down. Both characters otherwise match their sheets and the ch26 rows. Ponnan rides the smaller horse a head lower and Kayal has no markings. The shrine, the canal boats and the smoke match 5.2. There is no text and the hands are sound. Ponnan's balloon can sit over the vine tops at top left, and Nagoji's two balloons fit in the open sky and smoke at top right.

Usable. The memory faces are more solid painted portraits than the smoke-textured stain the script asks for, though they are muted, grainy and dissolve into the smoke at their lower edges. Revathi's grey threading is faint but present, and a pendant at her throat reads as the tali. Padmini is greyed, with the stick head beside her. The soldier wears a white turban, unlike the bare-headed riders in 5.1. A few distant structures burn beyond the canal, which is acceptable as the raiders' fires. Nagoji is correct on foot at an untouched green vine line, in the full uniform with clean chin and stud, and the scar is on his left forearm. Dry leaf litter is under his boots and the torch handoff hands are sound. There is no text. The caption fits in the open sky at top left.

Acceptable. The panel matches the beat: tight on the oil-cloth-wrapped torch held to dry leaf litter and bark at the base of a pepper support tree, with flame touching but nothing caught. Nagoji's face behind it is warm-lit and grim, waiting. He matches the sheet: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain, buckled boot. No text. Minor notes: under the torch, only the thumb of his second hand peeks out between the coat and the leaves, a small odd blob that is not distracting at print size. The torch flame licks a little way up the bark. Loaded boats sit on the canal in the background. Lettering: the single caption fits in the clear blue sky at the top left (x 0.06 to 0.38, y 0.02 to 0.16), away from his face and the torch.

Clean. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch25-27 row: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, sooty white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain, breeches and buckled boots. He steps back from the burning post with the torch raised, and white steam shows at the stem. Shrine, canal and pepper boats match 6.2 to 6.4. One nit: a faint pale smudge about 25 px wide on the inner right wrist of the torch arm looks like faint glyph strokes when zoomed 10x. At print size (1:1) it is only a tiny smudge. Optional retouch. No lettering is needed.

Acceptable. The beat reads: a raised view of separate post fires with gaps between them, Nagoji walking the row with a torch, and Travancore men (white mundu, crossed belts) lighting post after post on either side. His face matches the sheet (stud, clean chin, moustache, topknot, grey temples). The long thin white scar is correctly on his inner LEFT forearm. Minor continuity point: his coat has no soot here, although 6.1 shows soot 'already' on it. The Travancore men wear white head cloths. Their white mundu and crossed belts still set them apart from the raiders. Caption space is the smoky sky at top centre and right (x 0.38 to 0.95, y 0 to 0.07), above the canal treeline.

Acceptable. Fire has leapt from the burning vines onto a pile of fallen branches, with black smoke boiling up. Two Travancore men (white mundu, crossed belts) flinch back from the heat with sound hands and anatomy. The canal, boats and shrine continue 6.1 and 6.2. Minor point: two boatmen in the background (one poling, one seated in a boat) look unbothered by the fire. The long caption can sit in the clear blue sky at top centre-right (x 0.45 to 0.8, y 0 to 0.18).

Acceptable. Travancore musketeers kneel in a line at the edge of the burn and fire into the smoke. They wear white mundu and crossed leather belts, with no blue or red coats. Raiders show as dark head-clothed silhouettes against the flame under a plain, unlettered faded-green banner. Minor points: the raider silhouettes look like they wear tunics rather than bare shoulders. The locks read more like flintlocks than clear matchlocks, which is not noticeable at this scale. Caption space is the smoky sky at top left and centre (x 0.17 to 0.55, y 0 to 0.12).

Acceptable. This fixes the v01 rejection: both coat sleeves now reach his wrists, and neither the hauling hand nor the free hand has any scrawl, scar or marks. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch25-27 row: soot-streaked face, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, topknot, grey at the temples, a sooty white coat, red waistcoat with brass buttons, silver chain (the medallion has a vague engraving and no letters), knee breeches and buckled boots. He hauls a coughing Travancore man (white head cloth, white mundu, crossed leather belts) out of the smoke by his shoulder cloth. The hands are sound. Raiders behind him cough and stumble with arms over their faces, there are no bodies, and the plain faded-green banner has no writing. The pepper vines, canal, shrine and boats match 6.1 to 6.4. Minor points: (1) the two raiders at right are lit and detailed (bare-chested, indigo cloth, head cloths) rather than pure silhouettes, and one has a single cloth strap over one shoulder, not crossed belts. (2) Small background boatmen in orange head cloths load pepper calmly, the same oddity noted in 6.3. Space for both captions: the smoky sky at top centre (x 0.45 to 0.78, y 0.0 to 0.26), between Nagoji's hair and the banner and above the raiders' heads.

Minor: the distant survivors walk upright carrying spears and a long gun instead of limping. The wading figure's grey short-sleeved shirt, back straps and round cap look slightly modern, and the straps could be read as Travancore cross-belts. All of them are tiny at print size. Everything else is on script: a burned corridor through standing pepper, fallen charred posts, a dropped flintlock and a scorched plain green banner with an unlettered pale disc. There are no bodies and no text, and the sky across the top has clear room for both captions.

Minor only. Nagoji's face is broader and heavier than the sheet, with faint shading on the chin, but every identity marker holds: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud. The ch24 uniform is complete: white coat with soot-black cuffs, red waistcoat, brass buttons, breeches, boots and silver chain. He holds the brass cup at chin height with a sour sidelong look, which reads as the grimace. Varma is bare-headed with a knot, cream and gold, gold necklaces, on the far dais. Padmini stands in the side doorway with grey in her hair, soot on her sari and her stick. Soldiers in white mundu line the hall and turn toward her. Brass open-wick lamps. The map has no lettering and there is no painted text. The caption fits in the low-detail ceiling band at top left (x 0 to 0.45, y 0 to 0.13), above every head.

Minor continuity points. Padmini's sari is clean here, but the arrival wide (7.2) has soot on it. The 7.2 correction moves the soot to the lower sari, which the table hides in this panel. Varma's knot sits toward the back of his head, not clearly above his left ear. His platform backdrop is dark wood rather than the red cushions of 7.2. Padmini matches her sheet: grey threading, gold beads and studs, cream sari with a gold border, stick in her right hand. She looks straight down the lens at Nagoji with a flat face, and Varma is a lamplit figure on his platform behind her. The map is ink lines only. The balloons can go top centre to right over the roof beams and wood wall, above Varma's head.

Minor continuity only. Padmini's sari is clean here, but in 7.2 it is heavily soot-streaked; most of the streaking in 7.2 is below the hip, so the table hides much of the gap. The background soldiers wear white sleeveless vests with crossed belts, while in 7.2 they are bare-chested. Otherwise clean. The two-shot across the map table works: Nagoji on the left, open-handed and answering, and Padmini on the right, unmoving, stick and hand on the table. Varma sits on his dais behind them, matching 7.2. Nagoji matches the sheet: topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, sooty cuffs, chain of office. Hands are sound. The map is ink lines and palms with no lettering. Lettering: Padmini speaks first but stands on the right. Put her balloon high in the centre (about x 0.35 to 0.72, y 0.02 to 0.14, over the ceiling, pillar and doorway) with its tail running right. Stack Nagoji's below it on the left-centre (about x 0.33 to 0.55, y 0.15 to 0.30) with its tail running left. Both stay clear of Varma's head at x 0.62.

Minor background inconsistencies. A seated figure who resembles Varma wears a cream upper cloth with a gold sash and loose hair, and sits at the table level instead of bare-chested on his platform; he can read as an unnamed councillor. The guards wear white turbans with red sashes, unlike 7.2's bare-headed soldiers. The coat shows no soot, but the cuffs are out of frame. Nagoji himself matches his sheet and the bible row: thick curled moustache, a clean chin with only light hatching, small gold ear stud, grey at the temple, topknot, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. His troubled gaze toward frame right fits 7.2's geography, with Padmini on the right. There is clear wall, window and doorway space at upper right (about x 0.59 to 0.80, y 0.03 to 0.35) for both balloons.

Minor only. Padmini matches her sheet and the ch26 row: grey through her coiled hair, cream sari with gold border, old drape, stick. The soot visibly falls from her fingers onto the canal lines. The map is plain ink with no lettering, but it is untinted, while the maps in 8.2 and 8.3 have pale blue water. Her sari shows no soot smear, which matches 7.3 and 7.4. The dim dais at the back of the hall is empty, although Varma is on his platform in 8.3. Put the balloons over the ceiling and back wall at upper right.

Acceptable reverse angle over Padmini's shoulder. Nagoji is correct: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, grey at the temples, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, and a silver chain whose plain shield pendant has no text. His hair is a crown knot with long curls falling, the same as page 7. One continuity flaw: the red-cushioned royal seat on the dais behind the map table is empty, although 8.3 shows Varma seated there. Letter the two Padmini balloons in the upper centre between the two heads, over the ceiling and back wall; that also covers the empty seat. Padmini's mouth is hidden, so the tail points to her turned cheek.

Clean. Varma matches his V13 face and the war-hall look: bare-headed, a hair knot at the back-left of the crown above his left ear, bare chest, cream mundu with a gold border, gold necklaces, spear beside him, seated on his platform and unreadable. Padmini is half-turned toward him with her stick in hand. Soldiers in white mundu and head cloths sit along the hall. The map has pale blue water and no lettering. Put Varma's balloon on the ceiling band above him at upper right, and Padmini's two over the ceiling and door wall at upper left and centre.

Acceptable. Padmini stands at the doorway with her bare back to the hall, in profile toward the night outside, not looking round, her hand sound on her stick. Nagoji is small in the lamplight behind her: crown knot, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, chain, breeches and boots. The hall is now empty of soldiers and Varma, and the royal seat at the back is empty, which is a mild break from 8.3; it reads as her isolation. The map scribble has no lettering. Put the three balloons on the ceiling rafters and the back wall in the upper left and centre, clear of both heads.

Minor only. Nagoji has a light stipple of stubble on the jaw and chin. It is within the bible's 'light stubble at most' and matches 9.2 to 9.5. Two spear guards stand by the tower door, so he is not strictly 'alone', but they are distant, facing away and the same as in 9.2, 9.3 and 9.5. The blackened strip shows only as a dark band of distant trees with a bare clearing in front. That fits 'a dark line across the green' but is less obviously burned than the smoking strip in 9.3. Uniform, topknot, grey temples, ear stud, chain, Revathi's indigo sari, jasmine braid, grey threading, sandalwood line, tali and armlets all match. Hands are sound and there is no painted text. The open sunset sky between the tower and Nagoji (top left to centre) takes the caption and Revathi's balloon, and the sky at top right is also clear.

Minor only. Nagoji is walking beside her and glancing at her rather than turning at the parapet, but the panel still reads as him turning to her while she keeps walking. Revathi has a thin red line in her hair parting that is not on her sheet or in 9.3. Both principals otherwise match: Nagoji has a clean chin, curled moustache, gold stud, topknot, grey temples and the uniform with chain; Revathi has grey threading, jasmine braid, sandalwood line, tali, coin necklace and armlets. Open sky at top centre and top right for both balloons.

Minor. The background guards wear white head cloths, while in 9.1 and 9.2 they are bare-headed. Revathi stands at Nagoji's frame-left here, while 9.2 and 9.5 put her at frame-right. Faint smoke still rises from the strip a few days later, which reads as smouldering. The beat is correct: both lean on the parapet staring at the blackened strip and neither looks at the other. Hands are sound. Both match their sheets and bible rows. Wide open sky at the top for her two balloons.

Acceptable with one small detail flag. The pendant on the silver chain of office is a European-style crest: a crown over a shield with two rampant lion supporters. It is not text, but it could read as a European royal arms. At small-panel print size it is a grey disc, so a light retouch to a plain or conch-marked medallion is optional. Nagoji has light jaw stubble, consistent with the rest of the page. He looks off-panel right toward where Revathi stands in 9.5. Topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, ear stud, white coat, red waistcoat and brass buttons all match. The visible hand is anatomically sound. The open sky at top right takes the single balloon easily.

Minor only. Nagoji has light jaw stubble, consistent with the page. Background spear guards at the tower are the same as in 9.1 to 9.3. The script beat is met: Revathi faces the setting sun with warm last light on her face, and Nagoji stands at the left edge in uniform watching her. Her costume matches the sheet and the ch26 row (indigo sari with gold, jasmine braid, grey threading, sandalwood line, tali pendant, armlets). Hands on the parapet are sound and there is no painted text. The wide sunset sky from the centre to the right edge takes all three Revathi balloons without covering faces.

Minor only. Her torso still faces the camera, with only her head and eyes turned to frame right toward the off-panel Nagoji. 'Facing him fully' is softened, but it reads correctly because 10.2 puts Nagoji at her right. She stands beside the parapet rather than visibly straightening from it. There is a thin orange sindoor line in her hair parting, the same small mark she has elsewhere on the page. Everything the r1 correction asked for is fixed: the ink-and-wash rendering and muted lavender-gold sky match 10.2 and 10.3, she has clear grey threading, there is no nose stud, and the tali shows on its dark cord below the flat-coin necklace. Jasmine braid, sandalwood line, armlets, bangles and the indigo-and-gold sari are on model. The same tiled gatehouse and white-mundu guards with crossed belts stand at left, and the burned strip shows as a dark band on the land. Hands are sound.
